A zero-timeout poll on a pidfd: it asks whether the process has exited and returns at once, so it is no deadline and waits for nothing (the doc comment says it polls a pidfd, never a pty master, and an error reads as exited: fail closed). The rule's `bare-deadline` pattern matches the literal `0` in `poll(.., 0)`; the literal is the absence of a wait. Both h1f checkpoint reviewers ADMIT. A: A zero-timeout readiness probe on a pidfd: it returns at once, waits for nothing, and -1 reads as exited (fail closed: no signal). Both callers (linux.rs:1962, :2035) call it once per check on the way to a signal; no loop or sleep around it. Not a vendor branch; the bare-deadline match is the literal 0 that means no wait. B: libc::poll(..., 0) has a zero timeout and returns immediately; signal_with uses it to check pidfd state before signalling. The literal 0 is the absence of a wait, not a deadline, and the function names no vendor. rf3c: re-recorded from the rf3b reviewers A and B, who classified it the same way (their reports, Part 3 / Rust section).

R19: the pause between two reads of a process-table snapshot whose scan raced a change. 1 ms doubling to 16 ms and never past the caller's deadline (the two named constants above it). There is no event to wait on: the table is read again, so this is a rate limit, not a wait for a state. It names no vendor and sits on no vendor's path. Its production callers are the owned-snapshot loops linux.rs:642 and darwin.rs:565; posix.rs:1264 and :1275 are its own test (inside `#[cfg(test)] mod retry_tests`). Both h1f checkpoint reviewers ADMIT. A: Shared POSIX code with no vendor. The two production loops (linux.rs:642, darwin.rs:565) accept a table only when two consecutive reads are equal and end with TimedOut at the deadline, so correctness does not rest on the sleep: it is a bounded rate limit (1 to 16 ms, never past the deadline), not a wait for a state and not a sleep hiding a race. B: linux.rs:639-644 and darwin.rs:553-566 call it only after WouldBlock from a raced process-table scan. The 1 to 16 ms backoff prevents a retry spin and is capped by the caller's deadline; it does not select a vendor or replace a correctness check with an unexplained sleep. rf3c: re-recorded from the rf3b reviewers A and B, who classified it the same way (their reports, Part 3 / Rust section).
